newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Nintendo to post speacial loss in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Nintendo to post speacial loss in 1996/97.

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said on Monday that it would post a parent special loss of 26 billion yen ($208.5 million) in the 1996/97 year which ended in March to cover losses stemming from the rationalisation of its unprofitable European sales units.
"We decided to get rid of cumulative losses at our European units before we launch 64-bit videogame machines in the market," a Nintendo spokesman said.
The special loss is likely to drag down Nintendo's 1996/97 parent net profit to 35 billion yen, compared with its original projection of 48 billion yen made last November, Nintendo said.
Nintendo dissolved its Belgian unit and lowered the book value of its Dutch and French units, he said.
The yen's weakening and strong sales of its 64-bit machines in Japan and the United States, however, prompted Nintendo to revise upward its group profit forecasts.
Nintendo said it expected group net profits of 63 billion yen in 1996/97, up from an original estimate of 48 billion yen announced last November.
Nintendo also revised upward its parent current profit forecast to 100 billion yen, up from 85 billion yen, citing the favourable impact on its business of the weak yen.
Nintendo's parent operating profits may have climbed to around 55 billion yen, director Hiroshi Imanishi told a news conference.
Imanishi said foreign exchange profits during the year totalled an estimated 27 billion yen.
He said Nintendo shipped 6.12 million 64-bit game machines by the end of March. Of that number, the U.S. market accounted for 3.42 million, Japan 2.04 million and Europe 660,000, he said.
Imanishi said shipments exceeded the company's original projection by 120,000 units, but sales fell short of the target by 21.3 billion yen due to price declines.
Nintendo expects shipments of Nintendo64 players to reach 12 million units by March 1998.
